body.p: Claims 21-40 are currently pending. Consideration of the pending claims, namely, claims 21-40 is respectfully requested. By the present amendment, claims 30, 34, 37, and 40 are amended.

In the Office Action Examiner Kurr indicated that claims 25, 34-36 and 39-40 are objected to as being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims. Claim 22 would be rejected under Statutory Double Patenting if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims. Applicant's representatives extend our appreciation to Examiner Kurr for the recognition of allowable subject matter.
Claim 1, 23-24, 26 and 29-33 is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §102 as being anticipated Standley (US Patent 5,830,235; hereafter "Standley").
Anticipation requires a single prior art reference that discloses each element of the claim. W.L. Gore & Associates v. Garlock, Inc., 220 U.S.P.Q. 303, 313 (Fed. Cir. 1983),

cert. denied 469 U.S. 851 (1984). Additionally, the single prior art reference must disclose each and every element of the claimed invention, arranged as in the claim. Lindemann Maschinenfabrik GmbH v. American Hoist & Derrick Co:, 221 U.S.P.Q. 481, 485 (Fed. Cir. 1984). "There must be no difference between the claimed invention and the reference disclosure, as viewed by a person of ordinary skill in the field of the invention". Scriups Clinic & Research'Foundation, v. Genentech Inc., 18 U.S.P.Q.2d
1001, 1010 (Fed. Cir. 1991). "The identical invention must be shown in as complete detail as is contained in the ... claim".

Claim 21 recites, inter alia, providing an motor device comprising a sensor and a depressible portion producing an output signal when said depressible portion is compressed yielding a first measured pressure over an age appropriate predetermined threshold applied to the depressible portion.

Standley does not teach an age appropriate predetermined threshold, rather Standley merely teaches that "[t]he sensitivity control dial 25 is used to set the sensitivity of detection of pressure being exerted on a nipple 15 of the pacifier 13" (Col. 3, lines 45- 50). This does not teach applying a first measured pressure over an age appropriate predetermined threshold, as recited in claim 21. Standley teaches a guessing game, wherein a user adjusts a sensitivity control dial 25 to be "at a sufficiently low position to avoid having the tape player 35 play with just a slight pull on the pacifier nipple 15." (Col. 4, lines 2-5). As Standley does not contemplate basing the sensitivity of detection of pressure being exerted on a nipple 15 on the age of a child, merely referencing building a profile of a full term infant. (Col. 4, lines 30-31). Even when age is referenced in Standley, (twelve premature infants born at an average gestation age of 29.3 weeks and an average weight of 2 lbs. 4.8 oz.), Standley does not teach altering the pressure sensitivity based on those children's age. (Col. 3; lies 61-64). As such, applicant believes that claim 21 is novel in view of Standley, and notice to that effect is respectfully requested. Should Examiner Kurr disagree, they are encouraged to contact the undersigned to discuss.
Claims 22-29 depend from claim 21 and are allowable for at least the same reasons as amended claim 21 and/or for the specific features recited therein.

Claim 30 has been amended to include claim 34, which was indicated allowable by the Examiner. Claims 31-36 depend from claim 30 and are allowable for at least the same reasons as amended claim 30 and/or for the specific features recited therein.
35 U.S.C. &103 Rejections .
Claim 27 is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Standley in view of Mathew et al. (US Patent 9,369,537; hereafter "Mathew").

Claim 27 depends from claim 21 and is allowable for at least the same reasons as claim 21 and/or for the specific features recited therein. See In re Fine, 5 USPQ2d 1596, 1600 (Fed. Cir. 1988) (stating that if an independent claim is nonobvious, then any claim depending therefrom is nonobvious).
Claim 28 is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Standley in view of Kamm (US Patent Pub. 2008/0119108; hereafter "Kamm ").

Claim 28 depends from claim 21 and is allowable for at least the same reasons as claim 21 and/or for the specific features recited therein. See In re Fine, 5 USPQ2d 1596, 1600 (Fed. Cir. 1988) (stating that if an independent claim is nonobvious, then any claim depending therefrom is nonobvious).
Claims 37-38 is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Standley in view of Wild (US Patent 3,678,212; hereafter "Wild").
Claim 37 recites, inter alia, the motor device comprising a housing for a sensor, wherein the sensor produces an output signal when said housing is compressed to a

pressure over a first measured pressure over an age appropriate predetermined threshold; [...], wherein an interface, in communication with the audio device, displays an option to emit audio comprising at least one of a default recording, a non-native language recording, and a non-default read-song ratio recording to the use.

As discussed above with regard to claim 21, Standley does not teach an age appropriate predetermined threshold, as it does not contemplate age when determining a pressure. Further, neither Standly or Wild teach an interface in communication with the audio device, offering options to emit audio comprising at least one of a default recording, a non-native language recording, and a non-default read-song ratio recording to the use, as recited in claim 37. As such, applicant believes that claim 37 is novel and non-obvious in view of Standley and Wild, and notice to that effect is respectfully requested. Should Examiner Kurr disagree, they are encouraged to contact the undersigned to discuss.

Claims 38-40 depend from claim 37 and are allowable for at least the same reasons as amended claim 37 and/or for the specific features recited therein. See In re Fine, 5 USPQ2d 1596, 1600 (Fed. Cir. 1988) (stating that if an independent claim is nonobvious, then any claim depending therefrom is nonobvious).

Claims 21-40 are rejected on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 1-20 of U.S. Patent No. 11806122 B2. Applicant believes the amendments to claims 21, 30, and 37 overcome the double patenting rejections and
notice to that effect is respectfully requested. Should Examiner Kurr disagree, they are encouraged to contact the undersigned to discuss.

If any fees are determined to be due in connection with filing this Amendment or any other paper filed during prosecution of this application, the Commissioner is authorized to charge any such fees to deposit account no. 60-5050. If any extension of time is required in connection with filing this Amendment or any other paper filed during prosecution of this application, such an extension of time is petitioned for and hereby respectfully requested.
Respectfully submitted,
